implementation.versionBinding: read_visual calls the existing capture_expected with the full VerifiedFile; UI compares the full receipt and ties operations to file selection and active pane. No file URL grant or Agent access expansion.
implementation.image: Existing structural byte checks and browser image decode are reused. Decode cancellation retires UI ownership; a pending browser decoder may finish later and is ignored.
implementation.pdf: The official 6.3.289 legacy display library draws in the dedicated rendering Worker with OffscreenCanvas and a nested official parser Worker. No page DOM is created. Only fixed error codes, page count and a transferred ImageBitmap cross to the app.
implementation.warningPolicy: Both Worker contexts replace console.warn/error before library initialization and report only a fixed failure, without document text. stopAtErrors=false deliberately exposes recoverable parser errors as fatal warnings to Farfold. In 6.3.289 the stopAtErrors=true operator-stream path can settle rendering before reporting the rejection; the actual oversized-image fixture demonstrates this. Farfold never displays the recovered page.
implementation.fontCompleteness: After drawing, the exact locked PDF.js operator list/commonObjs font objects are checked for missingFile/isInvalidPDFjsFont, including Type3 nested lists. This closes the unembedded Chinese fixture that otherwise returned pixels with no warning. It is a version-specific library contract, not a proof of every possible PDF glyph.
implementation.noEvalClaim: The selected API has no isEvalSupported option. Farfold does not load a scripting manager or QuickJS asset. The official legacy build includes core-js compatibility code, including fixed global-object detection fallbacks; it is not correct to claim the entire bundle contains no Function expression. No document JavaScript is executed by the selected render calls. Packaged CSP omits unsafe-eval; actual WebKit CSP execution remains untested.

limits.meaning: Input/canvas/request budgets are not a hard cap on decoder/parser heap or OS memory. Worker termination retires the owned tree without awaiting a library reply; no instantaneous OS memory reclamation claim. File-read waiting uses the existing two-slot/15-second guard; it does not interrupt a blocking OS read.
